/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:36:## Usage limits
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:40:* **Guests** get a free daily usage allowance. Higher-priced models are greyed out in the mo
del picker with a "Sign in to use this model" tooltip. Sign in to unlock them. The sidebar shows a progress bar with how much of y
our daily limit you've used and when it resets. When you reach the limit, you'll be prompted to sign in.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:42:* **Signed-in users** get **10×** the daily usage of a guest. Your daily usage and any paid
credit balance are visible in the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:43:* **Paid credits** can be topped up from the billing page and are shown alongside your daily
limit in the account menu.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:44:* **Low credits warning**: when your credit balance drops to 10% or below, the sidebar credi
t meter turns red and shows a **Low credits** label.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:45:* **When credits run out**, only the free hosted models are locked. Models you access with y
our own API key (BYOK) remain available regardless of your credit balance.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:47:When your credit balance reaches zero, free models are grayed out in the model picker so you
can see the limit before sending a message. Models from your own API keys remain available. If you have paid top-up credits, free
models stay enabled even after your daily free allowance is exhausted.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:51:Open the **account menu** at the bottom of the sidebar (click your avatar or email) and choo
se **Sign out**. You'll be returned to the public app as a guest, and any signed-in usage allowance is replaced by the guest allow
ance until you sign back in.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:106:## Billing
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:110:The **Payment history** card on the org billing page lists your recent credit top-ups. Each
row shows:
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:121:To add credits, click **Top up**, either from the empty state when you have no history, or
from the credit balance card above.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:125:> **Free plan organizations cannot purchase credits directly.** If your organization is on
the Free plan, the Top up dialog shows a message that only an organization owner can upgrade the plan, with a **Compare plans** bu
tton. Clicking it closes the dialog and opens your organization's Plans settings so you can upgrade.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:133:Auto-reload buys credits automatically when your balance runs low. It isn't
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:137:* **Credits to add**: how many credits each refill buys, from 500 to 1,000,000.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:147:### Managing billing details
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:149:Organization owners on a paid plan see a **Manage billing** button on the billing page. Cli
cking it opens the Stripe portal where you can update payment methods, download invoices, add tax IDs, and review billing details.
Only organization owners can access this portal.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/hosted.md:153:When someone you invited to a paid-seat organization signs up and the automatic seat charge
fails or is cancelled, the org billing page shows a **Seat payment didn't go through** notice. As the org owner you can:
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/cli.md:335:Run the Cross-App Access (ID-JAG) debugger: self-issue an ID-JAG, redeem it at the target auth
orization server (RFC 7523), and call the MCP server with the resulting access token. See the [XAA Debugger guide](https://docs.mc
pjam.com/cli/xaa.md) for the trust setup, registration strategies, and CI usage.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/cli.md:569:An unknown ID, or an ID or flag for a suite the run leaves out, is a usage error (exit code `2
`) before anything runs.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/cli.md:597:| `--server <name=url>` | | Bind a target server to an HTTP(S) URL. Repeatable. Split on the f
irst `=`; duplicate or unknown names are usage errors. |
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/cli.md:611:Global `--timeout` bounds each setup operation and MCP request, not the whole run. Exit codes:
`0` passed, `1` failed, `2` usage/unsupported/import/policy, `3` credentials, `4` setup/billing/artifact, `5` inconclusive or int
errupted; see [Exit codes](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/local-evals.md#exit-codes).
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/cli.md:643:`--host` is a usage error rather than a silent precedence rule.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/cli.md:954:Launch a goal run. **Spends model credits**: fans out into `targets × iterations` chat session
s.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/cli.md:961:| `--expected-sponsored <n>` | No | How many of this launch's conversations you expect to be s
ponsored (paid from MCPJam's per-user allowance instead of your organization's credits). If the actual split differs, the launch i
s refused with a `409` and nothing is created. Omit to accept whatever split applies. |
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/cli.md:1209:Grade a saved server against a publisher's directory as the platform reaches it, through the
saved server row and the authorize exchange. This is the hosted half of `readiness check`: it answers a different question (what t
he platform sees, not what your machine sees), can optionally run a model for experience observations (included with MCPJam; no cr
edits are consumed), and leaves a persistent record.
/workspace/mcp-eval/docs/cli.md:1229:| `--ai-observations` | No | Add optional model observations. **Consumes MCPJam credits.** |

d. One of `lazy-authentication` or `enterprise-managed-auth`. Repeat to claim several (at most 10). An unknown value is a usage er
ror. |

le (after auth, before any server/model work) |

en that expired during a long poll). Zero credits spent if it happened before launch |
